events.title: Fortran 90 standard published (ISO/IEC 1539:1991)
events.summary: ISO/IEC 1539:1991 was published on July 1, 1991 — the Fortran 90 standard with modules, array syntax, and dynamic memory.
events.about: Fortran 90 added modules, array operations, `ALLOCATABLE`, and free-form source — a major modernization for numerical computing. Scientists could write `A = B + C` on whole arrays instead of nested loops. Modern Fortran (2003, 2008, 2018) builds on this foundation.

narrative.whyChosen: Fortran 90 was the first major rewrite since 1977 — array syntax and modules changed how HPC code was structured.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept Fortran dominant in supercomputing while absorbing ideas from other languages (modules, recursion, interfaces).
narrative.problemSolved: FORTRAN 77 could not express modern numerical algorithms cleanly; researchers needed array-level operations and reusable modules.
